items.q: Lung involvement (as opposed to renal involvement) occurs in what proportion of Goodpasture patients?
items.exp: Presentation flowchart: lung involvement 75% versus renal involvement 'as %', with renal involvement indicating a poor prognosis. (Book p782)

items.q: In Goodpasture syndrome, renal involvement is associated with a poor prognosis.
opts: False — only lung involvement affects prognosis
True only if the patient smokes
items.exp: The flowchart places 'renal involvement (as %)' with the note poor prognosis. (Book p782)

items.q: A young man presents with 2 weeks of cough and haemoptysis. He has no fever and no comorbidity. Which listed feature supports the diagnosis of Goodpasture lung involvement?
opts: Haemoptysis with no fever or comorbidity, in a smoker
Pleuritic chest pain with a pleural rub
items.exp: Lung features: history of smoking, cough, haemoptysis, and no fever or comorbidity — the absence of fever is emphasised. (Book p782)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed lung features of Goodpasture syndrome. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The book specifically notes 'no fever, comorbidity' among the lung features of Goodpasture syndrome. (Book p782)

items.q: Match the investigation with its stated result — 1) DLCO  2) X-ray chest  3) CT scan … A) ↑ (increased)  B) Diffuse alveolar haemorrhage  C) B/L diffuse infiltrate
items.exp: Evaluation: DLCO is ↑ (increased); X-ray shows bilateral diffuse infiltrate; CT scan shows diffuse alveolar haemorrhage. (Book p782)

items.q: The chest X-ray in Goodpasture syndrome shows a bilateral diffuse infiltrate, marked by an arrow in the figure.
opts: False — the X-ray is normal in Goodpasture syndrome
False — the X-ray shows a solitary cavitating lesion
True, but only after renal transplantation
items.exp: The chest X-ray figure is labelled 'B/L diffuse infiltrate' with an arrow pointing to it. (Book p782)

items.q: A patient with haemoptysis and RPGN has a CT chest showing bilateral ground-glass with dependent consolidation. The figure labels this:
items.exp: The two CT panels on the page are labelled 'diffuse alveolar haemorrhage'. (Book p782)

items.q: Which evaluation finding is NOT part of the Goodpasture work-up as printed?
items.exp: The DLCO in Goodpasture syndrome is increased (↑), reflecting the presence of blood in the alveoli; X-ray shows B/L diffuse infiltrate and CT shows diffuse alveolar haemorrhage. (Book p782)
